Keystone House, Inc. seeks a strategic, hands\-on Executive Director with demonstrated leadership and fundraising experience. The Executive Director leads a team of 35 full and part\- time employees and manages the organization's $3\.0 million budget. S/he must be able to oversee fundraising, programming, community relations and financial activities.

The ideal candidate must be able to build and maintain strong relationships with funders and other community leaders and have strong management experience. This candidate should also have expertise in mental health, specifically with adults with serious and mental health conditions, promoting the recovery model and demonstrating a passion for Keystone's mission.

Founded in 1972 in Norwalk, CT, Keystone House, Inc. began with one home that served 10 clients. The organization grew significantly over the years, providing behavioral health services to adults living with serious and persistent mental health conditions. For more than 50 years Keystone has promoted the recovery of its clients. No matter who they are, or what their background is, the goal is to help and support each client to live their best life and meet their personal goals.

**Major Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership and vision to ensure the effective operations and delivery of quality programs.

* Oversee and ensure compliance with and adherence to all contractual, accreditation and licensure requirements.

* Report to Board of Directors on progress of programs and financial status, ensuring their full engagement in policy making, governance and resource development.

**Experience and Qualifications**

* Previous management experience
* Successful fundraising and development experience

**Education**

jobs.description:
Community Access was founded in 1974 to provide housing and support for people being discharged from psychiatric institutions. Today, we are one of the leading providers of supportive and affordable housing in New York City, and the originators of an integrated housing model which has become a best practice nationally: affordable housing where families live alongside people living with mental health concerns. Our staff work daily to support thousands of New Yorkers through supportive and affordable housing, peer\-driven residential crisis support programs, training, advocacy, supported education, mobile treatment and other healing\-focused services.

  

**Department Overview**


The Housing department provides permanent and affordable supportive housing for individuals living with mental health concerns and low\-income community residents and families, as well as licensed transitional residential programs for individuals moving from institutions into the community. Services are geared towards assisting people in maintaining their housing and moving forward with their lives in stable community\-based environments.

  



**Position Overview**


The Assistant Program Director, in conjunction with the Program Director, provides supervisory oversight of the supportive housing program(s), including program leadership, staff development, service provision, community building, contract and budget management, and coordination with facility and property management. The Assistant Program Director supports the Program Director to ensure that services are provided within the scope of the agency’s mission and values and are consistent with the needs and desires of individual participants. * Ensuring that monthly policy reviews are completed with staff and documented in the Bridge Training Tracking system.
 **Job Qualifications**

* Minimum of two years of supervisory experience preferred.

For more than 50 years, WISE has been a steadfast advocate for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, stalking, and trafficking, while serving as a regional leader in prevention education, legal advocacy, restorative practices, and community engagement. Since its founding in 1971, WISE has supported more than 10,000 survivors, trained over 5,000 first responders and other professionals, taught healthy relationship skills to more than 18,000 students, and engaged more than 11,000 community members through workshops, education, and outreach.

At the heart of WISE is a belief that how the work is done is as important as the work itself. There are fundraising jobs. And then there are opportunities to help build something that could change the future of human health.

The American Brain Foundation is looking for an exceptional Director of Philanthropy to join us at a pivotal moment of our growth.

ABF is a premier national foundation advancing research across brain diseases and disorders. In 2025 alone, we committed more than $10 million to research. We work with some of the world’s most accomplished neurologists, neuroscientists, and scientific leaders to pursue questions that could change how we prevent, detect, understand, and treat brain disease.

As we expand our research investments, we also need to scale the philanthropic program needed to support that growth.

As Director of Philanthropy, you will have the opportunity to help shape ABF’s fundraising strategy, grow our major and principal gifts program, develop new philanthropic partnerships, and create opportunities for donors to invest in extraordinary science.

One day you may be working with a world\-renowned neuroscientist to understand their breakthrough idea. The next, you may be sitting with a family considering a seven\-figure investment in research that matters deeply to them.

You will work directly with our Executive Director, Board members, scientists, major donors, foundations, corporations, family offices, and other philanthropic leaders.
